subject: math
title: Addition and Subtraction Facts to 20: Doubles, Make Ten and Fact Families
seo_title: Grade 2 Math Addition and Subtraction Facts to 20 Worksheets (BC Curriculum, Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: Addition and subtraction facts to 20 (introduction of computational strategies)
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 math worksheets on addition and subtraction facts to 20: doubles, near doubles, make ten, fact families, turn-around facts, missing addends and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key, following the BC curriculum.
key_big: Learn your doubles and the pairs that make 10, and every fact to 20 gets easy.
body_html:
Doubles and near doubles

A double adds a number to itself: 6 + 6 = 12, 7 + 7 = 14, 8 + 8 = 16, 9 + 9 = 18.

A near double uses two numbers that are 1 apart. Use the double, then add 1.

Make ten

Two numbers that make 10 are a pair to learn by heart.

Makes 10Turn-around
1 + 99 + 1
2 + 88 + 2
3 + 77 + 3
4 + 66 + 4
5 + 55 + 5

To add past 10, fill a ten frame first. Then add the rest.

Example

What is 8 + 5?

8 needs 2 more to make 10. Take 2 from the 5. 3 are left. 10 + 3 = 13.

Answer: 13

Fact families and turn-around facts

You can add in any order: 8 + 5 = 5 + 8. This is a turn-around fact.

Three numbers make a fact family. If you know 8 + 5 = 13, you also know 13 − 5 = 8 and 13 − 8 = 5.

Example

What is 12 − 9?

Think: 9 + what = 12? Count up: 10, 11, 12. That is 3.

Answer: 3

Missing addends

For 8 + ? = 15, count up from 8 to 15. Do not count the 8 you start on.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting the start number: 9 + 4 = 12 (9, 10, 11, 12)Start on 9 and count the jumps: 10, 11, 12, 13
Subtracting the wrong way: 13 − 5 = 12 (5 − 3 = 2)You cannot take 5 from 3. Think: 5 + 8 = 13, so 13 − 5 = 8
7 + 8 = 147 + 7 = 14, so 7 + 8 is 1 more: 15
8 + ? = 15, so ? = 1515 is the total. Find the part: 15 − 8 = 7

faq.q: What addition and subtraction facts should a Grade 2 student know in BC?
faq.a: The BC Mathematics Curriculum for Grade 2 lists “addition and subtraction facts to 20 (introduction of computational strategies)”. Students learn strategies such as doubles and making ten, so facts like 8 + 7 = 15 and 15 − 7 = 8 become quick to work out.

faq.q: What is a fact family in Grade 2 math?
faq.a: A fact family is a set of facts that use the same three numbers. For 6, 9 and 15 they are 6 + 9 = 15, 9 + 6 = 15, 15 − 9 = 6 and 15 − 6 = 9.

faq.q: What are doubles and near doubles in Grade 2 math?
faq.a: A double adds a number to itself, like 7 + 7 = 14. A near double adds two numbers that are 1 apart, like 7 + 8: use the double 14, then add 1 to get 15.

faq.q: How can I help my child learn facts to 20 at home?
faq.a: Practise pairs that make 10 and the doubles for a few minutes each day, with fingers, coins or a ten frame drawn on paper. Then ask “if 8 + 5 = 13, what is 13 − 5?” so your child links adding and subtracting.

items.q: Each frame has 5 counters. What is 5 + 5?
items.e: This is a double. Double 5 is 10.

items.q: Each frame has 8 counters. What is 8 + 8?
items.e: This is a double. Double 8 is 16.

items.q: Each frame has 9 counters. What is 9 + 9?
items.e: This is a double. Double 9 is 18.

items.q: What is double 6?
items.e: Double 6 means 6 + 6. 6 + 6 = 12.

items.q: What is double 7?
items.e: Double 7 means 7 + 7. 7 + 7 = 14.

items.q: What is double 10?
Double what number makes 12?
items.e: 6 + 6 = 12, so double 6 makes 12.

items.q: Double what number makes 16?
items.e: 8 + 8 = 16, so double 8 makes 16.

items.q: Double 6 and 1 more. What is 6 + 7?
items.e: 6 + 7 is a near double. Double 6 is 12. The blue counter is 1 more: 13.

items.q: Double 7 and 1 more. What is 7 + 8?
items.e: 7 + 8 is a near double. Double 7 is 14. The blue counter is 1 more: 15.

items.q: Double 8 and 1 more. What is 8 + 9?
items.e: 8 + 9 is a near double. Double 8 is 16. The blue counter is 1 more: 17.

items.q: Double 4 and 1 more. What is 4 + 5?
items.e: 4 + 5 is a near double. Double 4 is 8. The blue counter is 1 more: 9.

items.q: Use double 3. What is 3 + 4?
items.e: Double 3 is 6. 4 is 1 more than 3, so add 1: 7.

items.q: Use double 5. What is 5 + 6?
items.e: Double 5 is 10. 6 is 1 more than 5, so add 1: 11. (1 is 6 − 5. That takes away.)

items.q: Use double 9. What is 9 + 8?
items.e: Double 9 is 18. 8 is 1 less than 9, so take away 1: 17.

items.q: Which double helps you work out 7 + 8?
items.e: 8 is 1 more than 7. Double 7 is 14, then add 1: 15. So use 7 + 7, then add 1.

items.q: Which one is a near double?
items.e: A near double uses two numbers that are 1 apart. 5 and 6 are 1 apart, so 5 + 6 is a near double. 5 + 5 is a double.

items.q: Harjot says 8 + 9 = 16. What did he do wrong?
items.e: 8 + 8 = 16. But 9 is 1 more than 8, so 8 + 9 = 16 + 1 = 17. He forgot to add 1.

items.q: Double 7 is 14. What is 14 − 7?
items.e: If 7 + 7 = 14, then 14 − 7 = 7. (21 adds instead of taking away.)

items.q: Double 9 is 18. What is 18 − 9?
items.e: If 9 + 9 = 18, then 18 − 9 = 9. (27 adds instead of taking away.)

items.q: How many more counters make 10?
items.e: There are 7 counters and 3 empty spaces. 7 + 3 = 10, so 3 more make 10.

items.q: How many more counters make 10?
items.e: There are 4 counters and 6 empty spaces. 4 + 6 = 10, so 6 more make 10.

items.q: How many more counters make 10?
items.e: There are 9 counters and 1 empty space. 9 + 1 = 10, so 1 more makes 10.

items.q: How many more counters make 10?
items.e: There are 2 counters and 8 empty spaces. 2 + 8 = 10, so 8 more make 10.

items.q: Which pair makes 10?
Which pair does NOT make 10?
items.e: 4 + 5 = 9, not 10. So 4 + 5 does not make 10.

items.q: What number goes with 6 to make 10?
items.e: 6 + 4 = 10, so the number is 4. (16 adds 10 instead: 6 + 10.)

items.q: What number goes with 1 to make 10?
items.e: 1 + 9 = 10, so the number is 9. (10 is the total, not the part.)

items.q: Fill the top frame first. What is 9 + 4?
items.e: 9 needs 1 more to make 10. Take 1 from the 4: 3 are left. 10 + 3 = 13.

items.q: Fill the top frame first. What is 8 + 5?
items.e: 8 needs 2 more to make 10. Take 2 from the 5: 3 are left. 10 + 3 = 13.

items.q: Fill the top frame first. What is 9 + 7?
items.e: 9 needs 1 more to make 10. Take 1 from the 7: 6 are left. 10 + 6 = 16.

items.q: Fill the top frame first. What is 8 + 6?
items.e: 8 needs 2 more to make 10. Take 2 from the 6: 4 are left. 10 + 4 = 14.

items.q: Fill the top frame first. What is 7 + 5?
items.e: 7 needs 3 more to make 10. Take 3 from the 5: 2 are left. 10 + 2 = 12.

items.q: Make ten. 8 + 5 is the same as which?
items.e: Move 2 from the 5 to the 8. 8 + 2 = 10 and 3 is left. So 8 + 5 = 10 + 3 = 13.

items.q: Make ten. 9 + 6 is the same as which?
items.e: Move 1 from the 6 to the 9. 9 + 1 = 10 and 5 is left. So 9 + 6 = 10 + 5 = 15.

items.q: Make ten. 7 + 6 is the same as which?
items.e: Move 3 from the 6 to the 7. 7 + 3 = 10 and 3 is left. So 7 + 6 = 10 + 3 = 13.

items.q: Start with the bigger number. What is 3 + 9?
items.e: Start with 9. Take 1 from the 3 to make 10. 2 are left. 10 + 2 = 12.

items.q: Make ten. What is 6 + 9?
items.e: Start with 9. Take 1 from the 6 to make 10. 5 are left. 10 + 5 = 15.

items.q: Make ten. What is 4 + 8?
items.e: Start with 8. Take 2 from the 4 to make 10. 2 are left. 10 + 2 = 12.

items.q: Make ten. What is 7 + 9?
items.e: Start with 9. Take 1 from the 7 to make 10. 6 are left. 10 + 6 = 16.

items.q: 8 + 5 = 13. Which is the turn-around fact?
items.e: A turn-around fact adds the same numbers in the other order. The total stays the same: 5 + 8 = 13.

items.q: 6 + 9 = 15. Which is the turn-around fact?
items.e: A turn-around fact adds the same numbers in the other order. The total stays the same: 9 + 6 = 15.

items.q: Use a turn-around fact. 4 + 9 = 9 + ?
items.e: 4 + 9 and 9 + 4 are the same. So the missing number is 4.
8 + 7 is the turn-around fact for 7 + 8. The total is the same: 15.

items.q: The frames show 8 + 5 = 13. Take away the blue counters. What is 13 − 5?
items.e: Take away the 5 blue counters. The 8 red counters are left. 13 − 5 = 8.

items.q: The frames show 9 + 6 = 15. Take away the blue counters. What is 15 − 6?
items.e: Take away the 6 blue counters. The 9 red counters are left. 15 − 6 = 9.

items.q: 7 + 5 = 12. Use this fact. What is 12 − 7?
items.e: If 7 + 5 = 12, then 12 − 7 = 5. Subtraction undoes addition.

items.q: 8 + 6 = 14. Use this fact. What is 14 − 8?
items.e: If 8 + 6 = 14, then 14 − 8 = 6. Subtraction undoes addition.

items.q: What is the missing part?
items.e: Whole − part = the other part. 16 − 9 = 7. Check: 9 + 7 = 16.

items.q: What is the whole?
items.e: The whole is the two parts added: 7 + 6 = 13. (1 is 7 − 6.)

items.q: Which subtraction matches the model?
items.e: Start with the whole and take away one part. The other part is left: 14 − 8 = 6.

items.q: Which fact is in the same family as 9 + 4 = 13?
items.e: A fact family uses the same three numbers: 9, 4 and 13. 13 − 4 = 9 uses them all.

items.q: Which fact is NOT in the fact family for 6, 9 and 15?
items.e: 9 − 6 = 3 uses the number 3, not 15. The others use only 6, 9 and 15.

items.q: How many facts are in the fact family for 5, 8 and 13?
Which addition fact helps you work out 16 − 7?
Count up from 9 to 12. What is 12 − 9?
items.e: Think addition: 9 + 3 = 12. So 12 − 9 = 3.

items.q: Count up from 8 to 15. What is 15 − 8?
items.e: Think addition: 8 + 7 = 15. So 15 − 8 = 7.

items.q: Count up from 8 to 17. What is 17 − 8?
items.e: Think addition: 8 + 9 = 17. So 17 − 8 = 9.

items.q: Simran says 14 − 6 = 8. Which addition checks it?
items.e: Add the answer to the number you took away. 8 + 6 = 14, so Simran is right.

items.q: Lucas says 13 − 4 = 11. What did he do wrong?
items.e: 13 − 4 = 9. Lucas saw 3 and 4 and did 4 − 3 = 1 instead. He took 3 from 4. Think: 4 + 9 = 13.

items.q: Find the missing number: 9 + ? = 12
items.e: Count up from 9 to 12: 10, 11, 12. That is 3 jumps, so the missing number is 3. (Do not count the 9 you start on.)

items.q: Find the missing number: 7 + ? = 11
items.e: Count up from 7 to 11: 8, 9, 10, 11. That is 4 jumps, so the missing number is 4. (Do not count the 7 you start on.)

items.q: Find the missing number: 8 + ? = 15
items.e: Count up from 8 to 15: 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15. That is 7 jumps, so the missing number is 7. (Do not count the 8 you start on.)

items.q: Find the missing number: 6 + ? = 13
items.e: Count up from 6 to 13: 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13. That is 7 jumps, so the missing number is 7. (Do not count the 6 you start on.)

items.q: Find the missing number: ? + 5 = 12
items.e: Whole − part: 12 − 5 = 7. Check: 7 + 5 = 12.

items.q: Find the missing number: ? + 8 = 17
items.e: Whole − part: 17 − 8 = 9. Check: 9 + 8 = 17.

items.q: Find the missing number: 5 + ? = 13
items.e: Whole − part: 13 − 5 = 8. Check: 5 + 8 = 13.

items.q: Find the missing number: ? + 9 = 16
items.e: Whole − part: 16 − 9 = 7. Check: 7 + 9 = 16.

items.q: Find the missing number: 14 = 6 + ?
items.e: The = sign means both sides are the same. 6 + 8 = 14, so the missing number is 8.

items.q: Find the missing number: 3 + ? = 11
items.e: Count up from 3 to 11: that is 8 jumps. 3 + 8 = 11, so the missing number is 8.

items.q: Find the missing number: ? + 6 = 20
items.e: 6 + 4 = 10, and 10 more makes 20. 4 + 10 = 14, so the missing number is 14. (4 only makes 10.)

items.q: Find the missing number: 11 + ? = 18
items.e: 1 + 7 = 8, so 11 + 7 = 18. The missing number is 7.

items.q: Find the missing number: 17 = ? + 9
items.e: Think: 9 + 8 = 17. So the missing number is 8.

items.q: Find the missing number: 8 + ? = 16
items.e: Double 8 is 16, so the missing number is 8.

items.q: Find the missing number: 12 + ? = 19
items.e: 2 + 7 = 9, so 12 + 7 = 19. The missing number is 7.

items.q: Find the missing number: ? + 7 = 10
items.e: 7 + 3 = 10, so the missing number is 3.

items.q: Find the missing number: 9 + 9 = ? + 10
items.e: 9 + 9 = 18. So ? + 10 must also be 18. 8 + 10 = 18, so the missing number is 8. (18 is only the left side.)

items.q: Find the missing number: 7 + 8 = 10 + ?
items.e: 7 + 8 = 15. So 10 + ? must also be 15. 10 + 5 = 15, so the missing number is 5. (4 comes from 7 + 8 = 14.)

items.q: Find the missing number: 6 + 7 = 7 + ?
items.e: You can add in any order. 6 + 7 = 7 + 6, so the missing number is 6.

items.q: Find the missing number: ? + 6 = 4 + 9
items.e: 4 + 9 = 13. So ? + 6 must also be 13. 7 + 6 = 13, so the missing number is 7. (13 is only the right side.)

items.q: What is 14 − 9?
What is 9 + 5?
items.e: 9 + 1 = 10, then 4 more is 14.

items.q: What is 16 − 8?
items.e: Double 8 is 16. So 16 − 8 = 8.

items.q: What is 6 + 8?
items.e: 8 + 2 = 10, then 4 more is 14.

items.q: What is 11 − 3?
items.e: 11 − 1 = 10, then take away 2 more: 8.

items.q: What is 20 − 7?
items.e: Think: 7 + 13 = 20. So 20 − 7 = 13. (17 comes from doing 7 − 0 in the ones. That subtracts the wrong way.)

items.q: Liam has 8 hockey pucks. He gets 5 more. How many pucks does he have now?
items.e: Add. 8 + 2 = 10, then 3 more is 13. (12 counts the 8 as well.)

items.q: 9 students are on the SkyTrain for a field trip. 6 more get on. How many students are on the train now?
items.e: Add. 9 + 1 = 10, then 5 more is 15.

items.q: Chloe picks 7 apples at an orchard in the Okanagan. Arjun picks 7 apples too. How many apples do they pick?
items.e: This is a double. 7 + 7 = 14.

items.q: 6 bald eagles sit in a cedar tree. 7 more eagles land there. How many eagles are there now?
items.e: Near double: double 6 is 12, and 1 more is 13.

items.q: 14 students are skating at the rink. 6 go home. How many students are still skating?
items.e: Take away. 14 − 4 = 10, then take away 2 more: 8. (20 adds instead.)

items.q: There are 16 rain jackets in the lost and found. Students take home 8 of them. How many jackets are left?
items.e: Double 8 is 16. So 16 − 8 = 8.

items.q: 12 orcas swim near the BC Ferries boat. 5 swim away. How many orcas are left?
items.e: Take away. 12 − 2 = 10, then take away 3 more: 7.

items.q: Mei reads 9 pages on Monday and 9 pages on Tuesday. How many pages does she read?
items.e: This is a double. 9 + 9 = 18.

items.q: Our soccer team scores 6 goals in one game and 8 goals in the next game. How many goals is that?
items.e: Near double: double 6 is 12, and 8 is 2 more than 6, so 12 + 2 = 14.

items.q: Ava sees 15 salmon in the river. Kai sees 9 salmon. How many more salmon does Ava see?
items.e: Find the difference. Count up from 9 to 15: that is 6. (24 adds them.)

items.q: The bus to Stanley Park has 20 seats. 13 students sit down. How many seats are empty?
items.e: Count up from 13 to 20: 13 + 7 = 20. So 7 seats are empty.

items.q: Some people are on the gondola at Grouse Mountain. 7 more get on. Now there are 16. How many were on it at first?
items.e: Take away the 7 that got on: 16 − 7 = 9. Check: 9 + 7 = 16.

items.q: Zara has 8 stickers. She gets some more. Now she has 15. How many stickers did she get?
items.e: Count up from 8 to 15: that is 7. Check: 8 + 7 = 15.

items.q: 11 students play outside at recess. It starts to rain and 4 go inside. Then 6 come out with rain jackets. How many students are outside now?
items.e: Step 1: 11 − 4 = 7. Step 2: 7 + 6 = 13. (7 stops after step 1.)
